children.name: GDP Nowcasting
children.blurb: GDP nowcasting is the estimation of a country's current-quarter gross domestic product before the official advance release.

children.name: Reading Central Bank Communication
children.blurb: Reading central bank communication is the systematic study of what monetary policy makers say and write, from rate decisions and statements to minutes, speeches, interviews and press conferences.

children.name: Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis
children.blurb: Synthetic populations for policy analysis are artificial datasets of people, households, firms, or places that match the statistical properties of a real population.

children.name: Climate and the Economy
children.blurb: Climate and the Economy in macroeconomic econometrics covers how weather shocks, gradual warming, and climate policy affect aggregate outcomes such as output, inflation, employment, investment, and trade.

children.name: Agent-Based and Game Theory Models
children.blurb: Agent-based and game theory models in macroeconomic econometrics study economies as systems of interacting decision makers rather than as a single representative agent.

sections.body: Macroeconomic econometrics is the part of economics that measures and forecasts whole economies, and AI is changing how that measurement and forecasting happens. Machine learning models now read high frequency data such as payments, shipping, electricity use, and online prices to estimate current economic activity before official statistics arrive. Natural language processing scans central bank statements, speeches, and minutes to score tone, uncertainty, and policy signals. Synthetic populations use statistical models to create artificial but realistic households and firms for policy experiments. Climate and the economy work links weather, emissions, and physical risk to growth, inflation, and fiscal outcomes. Agent-Based and Game Theory Models simulate many decision makers who react to one another, which is useful when equilibrium assumptions are too simple.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are relatively mature, especially short horizon nowcasting with rich data and text based measures of central bank communication. The hard parts remain causal inference, structural change, and uncertainty, because a model that fits past data can fail when a pandemic, war, or energy shock changes the relationships in the economy. Central bank language is subtle, and sentiment scores can miss conditionality, forward guidance, or deliberate ambiguity. Synthetic populations can protect privacy and fill data gaps, but their usefulness depends on assumptions and validation against real surveys. Climate and economy models must combine physical science, long horizons, and deep uncertainty, which makes precise forecasts difficult. Agent based models can represent heterogeneity and strategic behaviour, but they are often hard to calibrate and hard to compare with standard econometric benchmarks.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section form a chain from measurement to interpretation to simulation. GDP Nowcasting is the entry point for tracking current activity with mixed frequency data and machine learning. Reading Central Bank Communication shows how text analysis turns policy language into measurable signals. Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis covers the construction and use of artificial microdata for distributional and fiscal questions. Climate and the Economy connects environmental shocks and transition policies to macroeconomic outcomes. Agent-Based and Game Theory Models provides the toolkit for strategic interaction, heterogeneity, and out of equilibrium dynamics. A reader would go to the first two for short term monitoring, the middle two for policy design and structural questions, and the last for models where many agents react to one another.
